title: Rapid immersion SDK walkthrough - 15min to prod (notelet)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, opinionated lab for turning a curious engineer into a production-ready SDK integrator in ~15 minutes. Meant for: demo leads, field engineers, SDK authors, and PMs who ship onboarding experiences. This is intentionally terse — call it a pocket ritual.

Audience and success criteria:
- Audience: backend/frontend engineer who has a feature idea and 30 minutes to test it.
- Success: first working end-to-end request to Redwood API, embedded telemetry in app, and a minimal fallback strategy documented.

Constraints and assumptions (quick):
- Dev machine has Node 18+ (or Python 3.11) and Docker for the sandbox.
- Access token: user has a test API key in the org (ask sales/demo if missing).
- Network: outbound to api.redwood.ai allowed.

0-3 minutes: mental model and checklist
- Explain: "SDK = small, maintained client + templates + telemetry hooks + failure-mode guidance." Keep it simple.
- Quick checklist to complete before continuing:
  - copy API key to env var REDWOOD_API_KEY
  - make sure port 3000 is free for local sample app
  - open this doc and GH PR template (linked)

3-8 minutes: run the minimal sample app (Node)
- git clone github.com/redwood-inference/mini-sample-app (or use local starter template)
- cd mini-sample-app && npm i && export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk-xxxx && npm start
- Expected: web UI with a chat box and console logs showing token counts and latencies.
- Notes: if the app fails with 401, re-check token scope; if CONNECT_ERROR, toggle --insecure-temporary-flag (for demo only).

8-12 minutes: add a simple metric and a graceful fallback
- Add a counter for successful / failed requests (instrument code around SDK call). Pseudocode: increment counter before/after request; emit tag model=redwood-median-v1.
- Fallback pattern: if request latency > 1200ms OR error rate > 5% over 10s window, route to a cached reply (static response) and record a fallback event in telemetry.
- Why: demonstrates reliability controls + developer-visible economics.

12-15 minutes: smoke test and capture artifacts
- Trigger 5 concurrent requests (curl or load-generator script included).
- Verify traces: check local logs show token_time_ms and sdk_batch_size.
- Save artifacts: a short snippet of console output + one sample failing request and one successful fallback. Paste to PR description.

15-60 minute optional deepening (if time)
- Add prefix caching: cache prompt/response pairs for exact repeated prompts for 60s TTL. Measure cost delta in logs.
- Try a quantized model variant (if tenant has access): compare 90th percentile latency and cost-per-token.
- Add a simple canary rollout flag to switch between model variants via an environment variable and a tiny A/B counter.

Telemetry expectations and quick queries
- Minimal telemetry to record: request_id, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, outcome {ok|fallback|error}, sdk_version.
- Quick Kibana/Console queries to validate right after run:
  - errors last 15m by model_name
  - fallback rate across the sample app endpoint
  - avg token cost per request (tokens_out * unit_token_cost)

Common gotchas / notes to self
- Token stashing: devs copy/paste long keys into logs during demos. Add a sanitizer in example app.
- Local proxies: some corporate networks will intercept TLS; provide --proxy-ignore hint in lab notes.
- Silent failures: if streaming stops mid-response, check KV cache interaction and connection idle timeouts first.

Open questions / backlog items (unresolved)
- Should the sample app ship with a deterministic tiny LRU cache implementation or rely on the SDK built-in cache? (ENGDX-412)
- Short-term UX: show token burn in UI? pros/cons for demo clarity vs user panic.

PR/Deliverables checklist for converting this notelet into a polished quickstart
- [ ] convert pseudocode into 2 language samples (Node, Python)
- [ ] add unit tests for fallback behavior with CI smoke job (github PR linked)
- [ ] produce 1-min demo video and two-sentence README for marketplace listing
- [ ] add telemetry dashboard snapshot and link in README

Slack scaffold for live demos
- Pre-demo: post to #dx-demo with org name, short test token id, and start time. Use template: "Demo-ready: org=acme, app=notes, token=demo-123, start=14:00"
- Post-demo: paste artifacts + key learnings, tag eng-oncall if fallback invoked.

Tiny heuristics for copy and UX microcopy
- "We may take a second to think" (for initial model cold-start) vs cryptic error codes.
- Show explicit cost badge on the demo UI (approx tokens * unit cost) — helps align with product thesis re: inference economics.

Notes-to-self (rough)
- Keep the sample app under 200 LOC for easier comprehension.
- Add a one-click script to populate env + start Docker sandbox for offline demos.
- Consider a separate tiny deck (3 slides) for sales that matches the 15m flow.

If you use this notelet: please copy edits back to the GH starter-template (PR #237) and add a test ticket to ENGDX-412.

End of notelet.
